Jenna — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: marketplace purchases typically have a pass-through adjustment that affects the net revenue Redwood recognizes and therefore the applicable discount band; direct invoices let us offer the full committed-discount off the gross list. The tradeoffs are predictable billing vs. preferred unit economics.

Details below and I attached a one-page matrix and sample contract snippets. Key points:
- Direct invoice (best unit economics): Redwood invoices you directly, applies the committed per-token tier discounts against list, and the discount tables we publish apply. No marketplace fee pass-through.
- AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace (procurement-friendly): Marketplaces often apply a platform fee (5-15% typical). In practice we model two flows: (A) customer accepts marketplace list pricing and Redwood pays the marketplace fee out of gross (so effectively our net is lower) — to preserve our margin we either reduce the customer-facing discount or structure a rebate outside the marketplace; (B) customer takes marketplace invoice but we provide a separate Redwood-side credit/settlement — this requires a marketplace legal flow and is slower.
- Contractually: marketplace purchases require most customers to accept the marketplace contract and cannot be easily amended; any off-marketplace credits or passthroughs show up as separate statements.

Operational implications:
- Reporting and SLOs: Hosted metric SLOs and dedicated support are the same either way.
- Billing cadence: marketplace invoices are monthly via the vendor portal; direct invoicing can be net-30/45 as negotiated.

Next steps: if you confirm which path you prefer (Marketplace vs Direct), Lauren can run the discount model at your exact volume and Grace can confirm any SLO/commit language for the 12-month term.

- Marketplace w/10% platform fee (pass-through): marketplace list price increases to cover fee -> to hit the same effective economics we either need a deeper committed discount (we can offer incremental volume rebate of ~5% administered outside marketplace) or accept ~8% higher net to you.

Miguel — good question. Short answer: yes, in most cases we can migrate a customer from marketplace billing to a direct invoice without terminating production, but there are a few conditions:
- Marketplace contract restrictions: some marketplaces treat the marketplace subscription as exclusive; we coordinate with the vendor account team to allow a migration.
- Token accounting: usage needs to be reconciled so you don't double-count or lose credit; we perform a cutover at a clear epoch and reconcile consumption.
- Pricing lock: the direct-invoice committed discount can be backdated to cover the same start date if both sides agree in writing; otherwise it begins at migration.

Operational ask: please share the marketplace account owner and billing account ID (we will need to coordinate with AWS Marketplace support). I can own the migration plan and cutover windows.
